description: Remote Direct Memory Access decomposed. NIC reads/writes remote memory without involving the remote CPU. Verbs API (libibverbs, RDMA-CM). Queue pairs as the connection primitive. Memory regions + protection. Send / receive vs RDMA operations (read, write, atomic). RoCE vs InfiniBand. DCQCN for congestion control. Used in HPC, distributed storage, NVMe-oF, NVIDIA's NCCL for AI training.

sub_mechanisms.name: verbs_API
sub_mechanisms.definition: User-space library (libibverbs) for posting work to RDMA NICs. Queue pairs, completion queues, memory registration.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard interface across vendors. Applications call verbs to submit work; NIC processes it directly via doorbell mechanism. No kernel involvement on the data path.

sub_mechanisms.name: queue_pair
sub_mechanisms.definition: QP: an RDMA connection primitive. Has a send queue + receive queue. Multiple QPs per process possible.
sub_mechanisms.why: Connections are explicit data structures, not opaque OS objects. Application controls QP state, attributes, transport (RC, UC, UD). Direct access enables minimal-overhead communication.

sub_mechanisms.name: memory_region_registration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Application registers a buffer with the NIC: pins it in physical memory, gets a memory handle (rkey + lkey) for RDMA operations.
sub_mechanisms.why: NIC must DMA directly to/from the buffer. Pinning prevents OS from swapping it out mid-transfer. Registration is expensive (~ms for large regions) so applications register once + reuse.

sub_mechanisms.name: send_receive_operation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Two-sided: sender posts SEND, receiver pre-posts RECV. NIC matches them; data transferred to RECV buffer. Receiver's CPU is notified via completion.
sub_mechanisms.why: Familiar message-passing semantics. Receiver knows about each transfer. Used for control messages, small data. Not zero-copy on receive side (must pre-post buffers; specific buffer matched at send time).

sub_mechanisms.name: RDMA_write_operation
sub_mechanisms.definition: One-sided: sender posts WRITE with remote address + rkey. NIC writes directly to remote memory. Remote CPU is not notified (unless WRITE_WITH_IMM).
sub_mechanisms.why: Zero CPU involvement on receive side. Fastest mode: ~1-2μs latency for small messages on InfiniBand. Used for bulk transfers, distributed memory systems, AllReduce.

sub_mechanisms.name: RDMA_read_operation
sub_mechanisms.definition: One-sided: sender posts READ with remote address + rkey. NIC reads from remote memory + delivers to local buffer.
sub_mechanisms.why: Polling remote state without remote CPU. Used in distributed data structures, key-value stores (FaRM, RAMCloud). One-RTT remote read with no remote side intervention.

sub_mechanisms.name: RDMA_atomic_operations
sub_mechanisms.definition: Atomic Compare-and-Swap + Fetch-Add on remote memory. NIC implements these atomically.
sub_mechanisms.why: Distributed locks, counters, queues without remote CPU coordination. Performance vs CPU-based alternatives can be 10x+. Limited to 8-byte values; 64-bit atomic only.

sub_mechanisms.name: completion_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: CQ: queue of completion events. Each posted work request generates a completion when done. Application polls or waits.
sub_mechanisms.why: Async work model: post + check completion. CQ entries report success/failure + identifying info. Polling for completion gives sub-microsecond latency; waiting blocks until notified.

sub_mechanisms.name: reliable_connection_transport
sub_mechanisms.definition: RC transport: reliable, ordered, connection-oriented. Like TCP but in hardware. Default for most RDMA applications.
sub_mechanisms.why: Familiar semantics. NIC handles retransmits, ordering, congestion. The 'easy' mode for application developers. Connection setup is per-pair, so scales O(N²) for full mesh.

sub_mechanisms.name: unreliable_datagram_transport
sub_mechanisms.definition: UD transport: connectionless, unreliable. Like UDP but in hardware. One QP can send to many destinations.
sub_mechanisms.why: Scaling: N QPs for N hosts instead of N×(N-1)/2. Used by NCCL (NVIDIA collective communication for AI training) for AllReduce trees. Application handles reliability.

sub_mechanisms.name: DCQCN_congestion_control
sub_mechanisms.definition: DataCenter QCN. Receiver detects congestion via ECN-marked packets, sends CNP (Congestion Notification Packet) to sender; sender adjusts rate.
sub_mechanisms.why: RDMA's no-CPU model means software TCP-style congestion control isn't viable. DCQCN runs in hardware on the NIC. Standard for RoCEv2 deployments; required for lossless Ethernet.

sub_mechanisms.name: PFC_priority_flow_control
sub_mechanisms.definition: Layer-2 flow control: receiver tells sender to pause sending on specific priority class. Used to make Ethernet lossless for RDMA traffic.
sub_mechanisms.why: RoCE requires near-lossless networks (packet loss causes go-back-N retransmits, killing throughput). PFC enables lossless behaviour on Ethernet. Configured per-priority so only RDMA traffic gets the lossless treatment.

derivation_rules.name: RDMA_write_bypasses_remote_CPU
if: sender posts RDMA WRITE to a registered remote memory region
then: data is written without remote CPU involvement
derivation_rules.why: NIC has the rkey + remote address; it issues DMA writes directly to the destination memory. Remote CPU is not interrupted, no kernel involvement. This is the perf win: 100 Gbps sustained without consuming a remote core.

derivation_rules.name: memory_registration_is_one_time_cost
if: a buffer is registered once and used many times
then: the registration cost is amortised across operations
derivation_rules.why: Registration pins the memory + sets up NIC's translation tables — ~ms cost. Done once per buffer. Subsequent operations use the cached registration. Hot-path operations cost <1μs; cold-path includes registration.

derivation_rules.name: UD_transport_scales_better_than_RC
if: a process communicates with N hosts
then: UD's single QP outperforms RC's N QPs for scaling
derivation_rules.why: RC requires N×(N-1)/2 QPs for full mesh. With N=10K hosts, that's 50M QPs — exceeds NIC + memory limits. UD: each host has one QP that sends to any destination. NCCL exploits this for tree-based AllReduce in 10K-GPU clusters.

derivation_rules.name: RoCE_requires_lossless_network
if: RoCE is deployed without PFC + DCQCN
derivation_rules.why: RDMA's go-back-N retransmit is brutal: one lost packet retransmits the entire window. Modern InfiniBand uses selective retransmit; RoCE typically doesn't. Lossless Ethernet (PFC) + active congestion control (DCQCN) are required for RoCE to perform.

derivation_rules.name: polling_outperforms_interrupts_for_low_latency
if: application polls the completion queue continuously
then: latency to detect completion is microseconds
derivation_rules.why: Interrupt-driven completion: ~5-10μs per event (interrupt handling + context switch). Polling: ~1μs. RDMA applications poll CQs on dedicated cores for sub-microsecond message latency. Costs CPU but gives the lowest possible latency.
